clue.text: They'll accept a gamble, giving territory report to social workers

parts.note: turf is one's patch or territory
an account is a report of events
ants are social insects famed as workers

explanation.surface: Someone hands over land and a report to people from social services, taking a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social workers' looks like the care profession, but it means insects living in colonies. TURF ACCOUNTANTS is an old-fashioned British name for bookmakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers, formally called this in Britain, take people's bets, so they accept a gamble.

clue.text: Price, in electrical outlet, of an engaging piece of machinery

indicators.note: in tells us the price abbreviation sits inside the outlet word

parts.note: a socket is a wall outlet for plugs

explanation.surface: Someone asks the cost of a gadget plugged into the mains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaging' sounds like charming, but a sprocket's teeth engage with a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel whose teeth mesh with a chain, so it is a component that engages.

clue.text: Hit song's opening spot

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a mote is a speck or tiny spot

explanation.surface: A hit record's first bars land in exactly the right place.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic past tense of smite, meaning struck or hit.

clue.text: See 6
Daisy possibly married — no better afterwards

parts.note: iller, sicker, describes a patient who is no better

explanation.surface: A woman called Daisy marries, and afterwards things go no better for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afterwards' just places ILLER after M. Daisy Miller is the heroine of Henry James's novella; the puzzle's theme is famous people called Miller.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy Miller is a title character of Henry James, so Daisy is an example bearing this surname.

clue.text: Do another job: be a romantic singer of 5's theme song

parts.note: to moonlight is to work a second job on the side
to serenade is to sing romantically beneath a window

explanation.surface: Advice to someone with a night job: go and croon love songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenn Miller's band adopted this piece as its signature tune.

clue.text: Surrounded by light, though not by the sea

parts.note: in means enclosed or surrounded by
to light is to alight, to come down or land

explanation.surface: A lamp-lit place that is nonetheless far from the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like a noun for illumination; here it is the verb meaning to come down, as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Located away from the coast, so not beside the sea.

clue.text: "Where the forehead may be found?", as 5 co-wrote

definitions.text: Where the forehead may be found?
definitions.meaning: the forehead lies past the hairline's fringe, read literally
Jonathan Miller co-wrote this 1960s satirical revue

explanation.walkthrough: A FRINGE is British for bangs, hair cut across the brow; the revue was written by Miller, Bennett, Cook and Moore.
explanation.definitionFit: The revue's title read literally places the brow past the hair, and Jonathan Miller was one of its writers.

clue.text: Pipe stuffed with opium, as seen on TV

indicators.note: stuffed suggests the letters crammed together and jumbled up

explanation.surface: A pipe packed with opium, the kind seen in a television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' makes the anagram of PIPE and OPIUM. UP POMPEII was a British TV sitcom starring Frankie Howerd.
explanation.definitionFit: A British television comedy series, so the phrase points to something broadcast.

clue.text: Cat and what it will do on seeing mouse with no head

indicators.note: having no head means the first letter is dropped

parts.words: what it will do on seeing mouse
parts.note: a cat will pounce when it spots a mouse

explanation.surface: A cat and its reaction on spotting a headless mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no head' seems to describe the mouse, but it removes P from POUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also known by this name, so it is a big cat.

clue.text: See 23
Much earlier expanded silver ring

parts.note: long as in lengthened or extended
AG is the chemical symbol for silver
O is a ring by its shape

explanation.surface: An old silver ring that has been stretched.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock phrase for a time well back in the past.

clue.text: Fuel substance

definitions.meaning: the solid fuel left after coal is heated
slang for cocaine, a controlled substance

explanation.definitionFit: Both a smokeless fuel made from coal and street slang for the drug cocaine.

clue.text: Unbiased, thinking in terms of swings and roundabouts?

definitions.text: thinking in terms of swings and roundabouts?
definitions.meaning: with one's thoughts on funfair rides

explanation.walkthrough: A FAIR here is a funfair with swings and roundabouts; 'swings and roundabouts' is also a British idiom for gains offsetting losses.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial in judgement, and also, humorously, having one's mind on a funfair.

clue.text: Suckers, those who enjoy these popular pieces

definitions.meaning: sweets on sticks that are sucked
light classical favourites, a term popularised by Thomas Beecham

explanation.walkthrough: 'those who enjoy these' links the senses: suckers enjoy sucking the sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Both hard sweets on sticks and well-loved short classical works.

clue.text: Issue not allowed? Now look here!

parts.note: out means ruled out or not allowed
Come, come! is an exclamation of mild reproof

explanation.surface: Someone is told a matter is off the table, and protests.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a result or consequence, as in the issue of events.

clue.text: Divorce? Get ready to take your horse away

definitions.meaning: to separate a married couple, humorously

definitions.text: Get ready to take your horse away
definitions.meaning: release the horse from a cart or post

explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a horse from a vehicle, and jokingly to undo the knot of marriage.

clue.text: Stopped being a failure as a tear-jerker

definitions.text: being a failure as a tear-jerker

explanation.definitionFit: Both motionless and emotionally ineffective, failing to touch an audience.

clue.text: Lacking a true stem, roots or leaves, it'll do for cultivation (about half acre initially)

definitions.text: Lacking a true stem, roots or leaves

indicators.note: about puts the anagram round the initial letters
cultivating works the soil over, so these letters are turned over
initially takes the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A primitive plant is recommended for growing, given about half an acre at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cultivation' rearranges IT'LL DO to TLLOID; 'about' wraps that round HA, the first letters of half and acre, after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical term for plants like liverworts with a thallus body not split into stem, root and leaf.

clue.text: Hand to retreating crowd inside to get hold of an incendiary device

indicators.note: inside places the hand and crowd within the grabbing word

parts.note: to nab is to grab
the palm is the inner part of the hand

indicators.note: a retreating crowd goes backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

explanation.surface: A rioter's hand reaches back into a crowd to grab a firebomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb filled with jellied petrol, designed to start fires.

clue.text: Once put in an extra one of 5's trilogy

indicators.note: put in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: plus means an extra or bonus
ex means former, once

explanation.surface: Someone once slipped in an additional book of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Miller's trilogy The Rosy Crucifixion comprises Sexus, Plexus and Nexus.
explanation.definitionFit: Plexus is the middle novel of Henry Miller's trilogy.

clue.text: See 23
State force to secure a bit of an iceberg

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A state uses force to secure a chunk of a floating ice mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A calf is a piece of ice that has broken off a glacier or berg.

clue.text: Work of 5, as seen through a ship's captain's eyes?

definitions.text: as seen through a ship's captain's eyes?

explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Miller's play, whose title literally describes the outlook from a ship's command deck.

clue.text: One site associated oracularly with Apollo Theatre

parts.note: A is one, the indefinite article
Delphi was home to Apollo's oracle

explanation.surface: A place connected with Apollo's oracle, and the Apollo Theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apollo Theatre' reads as a single West End venue, but Apollo belongs to the wordplay; the Adelphi is another London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adelphi is a theatre on London's Strand.

clue.text: One who scored four times in a year with three short women

definitions.text: One who scored four times in a year

parts.note: Vi is a shortened Violet
Val is a shortened Valerie
Di is a shortened Diana

explanation.surface: Someone who hit the target four times in a year with three women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' means wrote music: Vivaldi's Four Seasons sets each season of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer of The Four Seasons, music for four times of the year.

clue.text: Palpitate and pong during flipping exercise

indicators.note: during puts the smell inside the reversed exercise
flipping turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: PT is physical training
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A heart racing and a bad smell during a blasted workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns PT into TP, and also reads as a mild British curse; HUM and PONG both mean a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: To thump is to beat hard, as a racing heart does.

clue.text: Enlivening drink taken with, say, backing band

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: eg means say, for example
a ring is a band

explanation.surface: A drink taken with a backing band to liven things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ginger something up is to make it livelier.
